query: I'm a working adult with a full-time job. Should I do my university degree online or in person?
concepts: cost differential between online and in-person
access to campus resources and professors
plausible_answers: Answer A (Online Default): Choose an online degree from an accredited university — for a working adult, the ability to maintain your income and schedule while earning a credential that employers now largely treat equally outweighs the networking disadvantages.

Answer B (In-Person for Networking Fields): Attend in-person if you're in a field where professional networks directly drive career outcomes (consulting, finance, law) — the relationship-building advantages of physical presence are worth the scheduling sacrifice.

Answer C (Hybrid Program): Seek a hybrid or HyFlex program if available — attending key classes in person while completing most coursework online preserves your work schedule while capturing the high-value networking interactions that purely online programs miss.
baseline_answer: Answer C (Hybrid Program): Seek a hybrid or HyFlex program if available — attending key classes in person while completing most coursework online preserves your work schedule while capturing the high-value networking interactions that purely online programs miss.
